transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Jordan Kim, Priya Menon, Ethan Lowe (Redwood) — Maya Torres, Omar Rizvi, Hannah Chu, Liam Park (Solstice)

[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick intro — i'm Jordan, i'm the AE working with Solstice, and Priya's our SE who will take you through the console.
[00:08] Maya Torres: Hi all — Maya here. we're mainly evaluating cost visibility and per-route controls, and want to understand how Redwood helps us find hot routes.
[00:15] Priya Menon: Great, yeah we'll start with a high-level tour then dive into per-route dashboards and cost. Ethan will jump in on batching and Optimize recommendations.
[00:26] Omar Rizvi: Quick note — we operate in a hybrid cloud, some tools run in GCP, some in an on-prem k8s and our compliance team is strict about data egress.
[00:35] Jordan Kim: Noted. we can talk about Private/VPC options and on-prem later in the call — Priya, over to you.

--- Console walkthrough ---
[03:05] Priya Menon: Opening the Console. Top nav: Routes, Models, Usage, Optimize. We'll open Routes. here you can see a list of routes — per-route TPS, avg latency, token volume and cost. For Solstice we'd map each API product to its own route so you can attribute cost to product teams.
[04:22] Hannah Chu: Can you show token-level cost? we need line-item chargebacks for FinOps.
[04:28] Priya Menon: Yep — click a route, there's a cost tab. It shows token breakdown: input vs output tokens, model used, quantization profile, and estimated spend over time. here you can group by HTTP path or user-agent. also exportable CSV.
[05:10] Liam Park: How accurate is the cost model vs AWS invoicing? we need to reconcile.
[05:15] Ethan Lowe: Good question. we derive unit costs from actual model throughput measurements and amortized GPU price; generally within a few percent of infra bills but we recommend a reconciliation job. we provide an attribution report you can map to your cloud billing ids.
[05:40] Maya Torres: Do you handle burst credits or reserved capacity visibility?
[05:45] Priya Menon: Yes — Dedicated shows reserved commit utilization and burst pools; you can set autoscale and see overcommit headroom. in hosted mode we show per-tenant quotas and throttles.

[08:00] Priya Menon: Next the Usage Explorer — time series of requests, tokens, and cost with filters for model, route, user tag. Very useful for anomaly detection. You can pin queries, save dashboards and set alerts on token spend or latency regressions.
[09:12] Omar Rizvi: We have some routes with very skewed sequence length distribution; batching helps but how do you avoid latency spikes for short tail requests?
[09:22] Ethan Lowe: We use latency SLO-aware batching; short requests get priority and we keep batch windows tight. Optimize suggests batching config per-route based on your actual sequence length histogram.
[09:35] Maya Torres: Show me Optimize.
[09:38] Priya Menon: Optimize tab — we run heuristic and sampling-based sims against your workload. recommendations: enable KV caching for prefix-heavy flows, reduce max tokens for certain assistant routes, quantize to int8 for non-critical routes, and route large-batch jobs to cheaper model variants. each recommendation shows estimated delta in cost and expected quality impact.
[10:12] Hannah Chu: Any examples or case studies?
[10:15] Priya Menon: yes — a retail customer reduced per-token spend by 36% by combining prefix caching and int8 quantization for non-critical inference paths. we can share the anonymized playbook.

--- Security & Deployment ---
[13:20] Jordan Kim: quick security note — Private offers a customer-managed control plane, VPC peering, and HSM/KMS integration. we also provide audit logs and token-level tracing for compliance purposes.
[13:45] Hannah Chu: Is SOC 2 and ISO on your compliance list?
[13:49] Jordan Kim: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 are included in the packet I'll send. we also support SAML SSO and RBAC.
[14:05] Omar Rizvi: For on-prem we need an air-gapped option — are there packaging constraints?
[14:10] Priya Menon: yes, we have an on-prem bundle for regulated customers; it includes the private runtime and offline upgrade methods. we'll follow up with the engineering checklist.

--- Deep dive: Example route diagnostics ---
[18:00] Priya Menon: opening a route diagnostics view — timeline of 95/99 latency, top prompt templates, token heatmap. you can replay traces for specific requests. here's an example where a hot prompt caused a 3x token increase on checkout-flow.
[19:04] Omar Rizvi: can we set per-route fallback policies? for instance, if model A degrades, go to a cheaper but compatible model B.
[19:12] Ethan Lowe: Absolutely. routing policies support priority lists and automatic fallbacks; you can bind them to latency or error thresholds and even regional preferences.

[22:30] Maya Torres: about deployment cost — if we run Dedicated for high-throughput checkout routes and Hosted for low-volume personalization, can we get cross-environment visibility?
[22:42] Priya Menon: Yes, the console normalizes and shows unified telemetry across hosted, dedicated, and private. you can filter by deployment type to see blended cost.

--- Objections & tradeoffs ---
[25:00] Liam Park: We're concerned about vendor lock-in if we adopt Redwood-specific routing and caching primitives.
[25:08] Jordan Kim: fair concern. we've tried to make primitives portable — configs are exportable and we document how to map to upstream infra. also, open model variants are supported so you don't have to stay tied to a proprietary stack.
[26:00] Hannah Chu: latency vs cost tradeoff — how do you help teams tune?
[26:06] Ethan Lowe: Optimize provides a cost-latency frontier per-route. it will show pareto points: e.g., quantize + aggressive batching saves 45% but increases 99th pct by 30ms; you pick the acceptable point and we can run A/B rollout on that route.

--- Live question from Maya ---
[30:20] Maya Torres: if we wanted to pilot with 3 critical routes, what's a reasonable timeline and what do you need?
[30:28] Jordan Kim: Typical pilot is 3–4 weeks: week 0 onboarding + corpus upload, week 1 perf run and Optimize baseline, week 2 iterative tuning, week 3 handoff. we need sample traffic, SLOs, and a point person for infra access.
[31:05] Omar Rizvi: access — do you need our keys? how does data residency work for logs?
[31:12] Priya Menon: For hosted we ingest telemetry but you can opt to forward logs to your SIEM; for Private, telemetry stays in your VPC and we provide an agent to ship only metrics if desired. keys are customer-managed in Private via KMS.

--- Wrap up and recap ---
[40:00] Jordan Kim: quick recap: we'll share SOC2/security packet, pricing and Dedicated sizing, and run the perf benchmark with your sample payloads. Priya will own the benchmark.
[40:20] Priya Menon: Action item: Priya runs perf with 3 routes and posts results. will include Optimize sims and suggested configs.
[40:30] Maya Torres: Thanks, this was helpful. Hannah will coordinate billing and PO details.
[40:40] Hannah Chu: yes i'll loop finance and get back on procurement timeline.
[41:00] Jordan Kim: i'll schedule pilot kickoff tentatively for 2028-03-28. any final q's?
[41:10] Liam Park: none from me.
[41:12] Omar Rizvi: all good.
[41:15] Jordan Kim: great — thanks everyone.

[End of recording — rough transcript; some speaker labels may be off, occasional transcription errors present]
